summary: Iteration 121: validated the server-side meta injection work. ALL 24 requested test cases PASS — GET /api/ssr/meta returns unique, page-specific title/description/canonical for every path (DB-backed and path-derived fallback), canonical is always self-referencing and never falls back to https://brightluxx.com/, unknown paths produce readable titles, and prerender-server.js injects title/description/canonical/OG/Twitter tags into <head> for ALL browser requests with X-SSR-Meta: injected. Verified across 42 routes: 0/42 had a wrong title, wrong canonical, or missing header. Regressions all pass (health, admin login via API + browser, products without _id, disposable-email rejection, /, /products, /contact, /technology, /calculator all render with unique document titles and no JS errors). pytest: 64/76 passed. HOWEVER, testing beyond the requested scope uncovered a CRITICAL pre-existing SEO defect that cancels out this fix for ~21% of the site: the crawler branch in prerender-server.js returns a hard 404 + X-Robots-Tag: noindex for live routes missing from its stale KNOWN_ROUTES/DYNAMIC_PATTERNS lists. 40 of the 191 URLs in the sitemap return 404 to Googlebot, and 39 of those 40 are real React routes. Also, the noscript H1 replacement regex never matches, so the initial-HTML H1 is still the same generic string on every page — the exact GSC complaint that motivated this work is only half fixed.

minor.issue: Site-name suffix is appended unconditionally, so DB titles that already contain the brand get it twice: / -> 'Brightluxx LED Display Solutions UAE | Digital Signage | Brightluxx', /products -> 'Brightluxx LED Displays & Digital Signage Products | Brightluxx'. Same for og_title. Skip the suffix when meta_title already contains 'Brightluxx'.

Several DB-backed titles exceed ~60 chars and will be truncated in SERPs (e.g. /technology = 'LED Display Technologies | MicroLED, COB, Transparent Dubai | Brightluxx' = 72 chars). Consider trimming the suffix when title length > 55.

PATH_TITLES advertises paths that have no React route (e.g. /for-contractors, /technology/cob, /technology/gob, /technology/hdr, /technology/driving-ic) — the endpoint happily returns indexable meta for non-existent pages. Prune or align with App.js.
_meta_cache is unbounded and keyed on arbitrary user-supplied paths, so any crawler hitting random URLs grows it without limit. Add a size cap or TTL.
Mixed and/or without parentheses: `if not c or c == PROD+'/' and path != '/'`. Behaviour happens to be correct due to precedence, but it is unreadable and fragile — add explicit parentheses.

ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL SEO: Googlebot gets HTTP 404 + 'X-Robots-Tag: noindex' for live routes that are missing from the hardcoded allow-list. 40/191 sitemap URLs 404 for Googlebot; 39 of them are real React routes. Confirmed 404: /technology, /technology/microled|cob-led|mip-led|fine-pitch-led|all-in-one-dvled|transparent-led|3d-anamorphic-led|creative-led|media-facade, /solutions/retail, /solutions/corporate, /solutions/control-rooms, /calculator, /viewing-distance, /power-estimator, /led-module-calculator, /project-planner, /technology-selector, /value-engineering, /spec-substitution, /installation-guide, /sla-guide, /distribution, /supplier-registration, /technical-support, /compare, /compare-brands, /government-solutions, /glassmorph/switchable-glass, /glassmorph/hanging-led, /tools/roi-calculator, /lp/specifier-toolkit, /latest-tech/*, /digital-experience/*, /contractors/*. Regular browsers get 200, so this is invisible without a crawler UA.

Regex /<noscript><div><h1>[^<]*<\/h1>/ has no whitespace tolerance but public/index.html has newlines + indentation between the tags, so the H1 is NEVER replaced. Every page's initial HTML still contains the identical noscript H1 'Brightluxx — Premium LED Display Solutions in Dubai, UAE'. This is exactly the 'identical H1 on all 182 pages' finding from GSC and it is still unfixed for non-crawler fetches. Use /<noscript>\s*<div>\s*<h1>[\s\S]*?<\/h1>/ or inject a data-ssr-h1 marker.

Crawler responses set X-Prerendered: true but NOT X-SSR-Meta, and they use injectMeta() (prerender.meta) instead of /api/ssr/meta. Two divergent meta code paths means crawlers and browsers can receive different titles/canonicals for the same URL. Consolidate onto /api/ssr/meta.

Crawler branch builds canonical from PROD_URL = REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL, which is the preview host in this environment. It happens to resolve to brightluxx.com only because .env points there; if the preview URL is ever used, crawler canonicals would leak the preview domain. The browser branch correctly uses the backend-supplied canonical.

Every HTML request now blocks on a full buffered fetch of the CRA page plus a backend round-trip before any bytes are sent (no streaming), and Content-Length is recomputed. Adds latency/TTFB on every page load; there is no cache on this path (the crawler path has one). Consider reusing prerenderCache for the SSR-meta path.

issues: Two H1s appear in crawler-prerendered HTML: the generic noscript H1 followed by the real page H1 — Google will read the generic one first. Fix the noscript replacement or drop the noscript H1.

action_items: CRITICAL: stop 404ing real routes for crawlers. Either delete the isCrawler 404 gate in prerender-server.js, or derive KNOWN_ROUTES from App.js / the sitemap instead of a hand-maintained Set. At minimum add: /technology + /technology/:techId, /solutions/:id, /latest-tech/:slug, /digital-experience/:slug, /contractors/:slug, /calculator, /viewing-distance, /power-estimator, /project-planner, /technology-selector, /value-engineering, /spec-substitution, /installation-guide, /sla-guide, /distribution, /supplier-registration, /technical-support, /compare, /compare-brands, /government-solutions, /glassmorph/switchable-glass, /glassmorph/hanging-led, /tools/roi-calculator, /lp/specifier-toolkit. Verify with: pytest tests/test_iteration121_ssr_meta.py -k must_not_404
Remove /led-module-calculator from the sitemap (no React route exists) or add the route.
Fix the noscript H1 regex so the H1 is whitespace-tolerant and actually page-specific (currently identical on all pages).
Do not append ' | Brightluxx' when the DB meta_title already contains 'Brightluxx' (title + og_title).
Unify the crawler and browser meta paths on /api/ssr/meta so both emit X-SSR-Meta and identical canonicals; make the crawler canonical use the backend value instead of REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL.
Add parentheses to the canonical fallback condition in ssr_meta.py:176 and bound _meta_cache.
critical_code_review_comments: A hardcoded allow-list of routes inside the proxy is the root cause of the 404s and will silently rot on every new page; generate it from the router or the sitemap.

HTML string-replacement injection silently no-ops when the regex does not match (noscript H1 proved this). Assert after each replace, or fail loudly / log, so a mismatch is caught in CI rather than by GSC.

Two independent meta-injection implementations (injectMeta for crawlers, inline block for browsers) duplicate ~80 lines and already diverge in canonical source and response headers — DRY violation with real SEO consequences.
prerender-server.js is ~690 lines mixing redirects, 404 logic, prerender, meta injection, proxy and WS upgrade; split into modules.

rca_of_the_issue: Two independent root causes. (1) Crawler 404s: prerender-server.js gates crawler requests through a hand-maintained KNOWN_ROUTES Set plus 6 DYNAMIC_PATTERNS and returns 404 + noindex for anything else (lines 437-444). The list was written before /technology/:techId, /solutions/:id, /latest-tech/:slug, /digital-experience/:slug, /contractors/:slug and ~20 standalone tool/landing routes were added, so Googlebot receives 404 for 40 of the 191 sitemap URLs while browsers get 200 — the new meta injection never runs for those pages. Reproduce: `curl -sI -A 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Googlebot/2.1)' https://brightluxx-catalog.preview.emergentagent.com/technology` -> 404 + X-Robots-Tag: noindex, while the same URL with a Chrome UA returns 200 with X-SSR-Meta: injected. Mitigation: derive the route allow-list from App.js/sitemap or drop the 404 gate. (2) noscript H1: the replacement regex requires `<noscript><div><h1>` with zero whitespace, but public/index.html:127-129 has newlines and indentation, so String.replace silently matches nothing and every page keeps the generic H1. Reproduce: fetch any path and grep the noscript block — it is byte-identical across /, /products, /technology/cob-led, /calculator. Mitigation: make the regex whitespace-tolerant and assert that the replacement occurred.
